!19 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: this source is compiled four times -- `vs_6_0` on two DXC versions, then\0A// `ps_6_0` on the same two versions, with the same waterfall-loop body (WaveReadLaneFirst +\0A// conditional break around a resource load).\0A//\0A// In the `ps_6_0` panes, the loop keeps a phi-based accumulator and the resource load stays\0A// inside the loop, guarded by an extra branch fed from a module-level internal constant array\0A// declared just before `define void @main()`. In the `vs_6_0` panes there is no such constant,\0A// no extra guard branch, and no accumulator phi: the resource load and its dependent input load\0A// are hoisted out of the loop into a single straight-line pass. Same source, same optimizer,\0A// different shader stage -- only the stage changes which shape comes out.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// From issue #5302 (verbatim, with the reporter's own compile lines kept as comments):\0A// dxc /Tps_6_0 .\5Cbreak.hlsl /DOUTPUT=SV_Target\0A// dxc /Tvs_6_0 .\5Cbreak.hlsl /DOUTPUT=Z\0AStructuredBuffer<int> mainBuf[]: register(t2, space0);\0A\0A[RootSignature(\22DescriptorTable(SRV(t2, numDescriptors=UNBOUNDED))\22)]\0Aint main(int a : A, int b : B, int c : C) : OUTPUT\0A{\0A  int res = 0;\0A\0A  for (;;) {\0A      int u = WaveReadLaneFirst(a);\0A      if (a == u) {\0A          res += mainBuf[u][b];\0A          break;\0A        }\0A    }\0A  return res;\0A}\0A"}
